title: AC vs DC charging
hook: AC vs DC charging, finally explained
caption:
AC charger, DC charger, onboard charger, kW... EV charging jargon can feel like a networking exam. ⚡

Here's the simple version:
Your battery stores DC. Grid power is AC. The only question is WHO converts it. If the car does it, that's AC charging (slower). If the station does it, that's DC fast charging (much quicker).

What do you use more, home charging or public fast chargers? Comment below 👇

slides.heading: AC vs DC charging, finally explained
Your battery only stores DC
slides.body: Grid power is AC. Something has to convert it.

slides.heading: AC charging: the car converts
slides.body: Its onboard charger does the work. Slower, ideal overnight.

slides.heading: DC fast charging: the station converts
slides.body: Power goes almost straight to the battery. Much faster.

slides.heading: Why it slows after 80%
slides.body: Charging tapers to protect the battery.

slides.heading: Best habit for most owners
slides.body: AC at home daily. DC on road trips.
